interactive_questions.title: Importance of Lock Concept
interactive_questions.question: Explore the critical importance of Locks in preventing concurrent data race conditions.
interactive_questions.explanation: Threads share the same memory space. When multiple threads try to mutate the same variable concurrently, their read-modify-write operations can overlap. This is called a race condition and leads to data corruption. Locks (or Mutexes) solve this by ensuring only one thread can enter the critical section at a time.

explanation_steps.description: Consider a 'balance' of 100. Two threads simultaneously attempt to add 50. If they read the balance at the exact same moment, both read 100.
explanation_steps.code:
# Thread A reads: balance = 100
# Thread B reads: balance = 100

explanation_steps.description: They both calculate 100 + 50 = 150, and write back 150. Despite two 50 deposits, the final balance is 150 instead of 200. We lost data!
explanation_steps.code:
# Thread A writes: balance = 150
# Thread B writes: balance = 150  <-- Data corruption!

explanation_steps.description: By putting the mutation inside a Lock, we serialize access. Thread B must wait for Thread A to finish its read-modify-write cycle before B is allowed to read the balance.
explanation_steps.code:
lock.acquire()
try:
    # Only 1 thread can be here at a time
    balance += 50
finally:
    lock.release()

interactive_questions.question: Analyze how database transactions ensure Atomicity in Python using try-except transaction boundaries, and complete the code.
interactive_questions.explanation: Atomicity guarantees that all database updates within a transaction are completed successfully as a single cohesive unit. If any individual operation fails, the entire transaction is rolled back, leaving the database completely unchanged.

Perform write operations, and run a commit if everything finishes without errors.
If an exception is raised, execute a rollback to undo any partial changes, saving the database from an incomplete state.

interactive_questions.explanation: Isolation guarantees that concurrent execution of transactions leaves the database in the same state as if they were executed sequentially. Uncommitted writes from one transaction must remain invisible to other concurrent transaction processes.

explanation_steps.description: Start an immediate write transaction on connection 1, securing an exclusive lock.
Connection 2 tries to read or write, but faces isolation barriers or busy locking conditions until Connection 1 commits.

# In isolation environments, Thread 2 sees old data

qty_result = cursor2.[[SLOT1]]()[[SLOT2]]

interactive_questions.title: Durability: Surviving Crashes
interactive_questions.question: Configure SQLite journal settings to secure durability properties in Python, and complete the code.
interactive_questions.explanation: Durability ensures that once a transaction commits, it remains saved in non-volatile memory or storage, even in the event of a sudden power outage, system crash, or system failure. SQLite achieves this by writing transactions to write-ahead logs (WAL) or rollback journals and syncing them to the storage disk.

explanation_steps.description: Configure SQLite connection to use WAL (Write-Ahead Log) mode to boost concurrently writing speeds and durability.
Instruct the backend engine to fully flush and synchronize cache pages physically to storage on commit.

snippets.title: Configuring Durability Levels
snippets.template:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect('vault.db')

# Enable Write-Ahead Log journal system
conn.execute('PRAGMA [[SLOT1]] = WAL')

# Ensure secure synchronization settings on every commit
conn.execute('PRAGMA [[SLOT2]] = NORMAL')

# Modifications committed below are legally written to [[SLOT3]]
conn.execute("INSERT INTO gold_vault VALUES ('vault_A', 5000)")
conn.commit()
snippets.code_reasoning: Using WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) coupled with robust synchronous settings forces SQLite to flush transaction records directly onto the physical storage disk on commit. Even if the hardware loses power immediately after, the logs remain retrievable and unharmed on reboot.
snippets.correct_code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect('vault.db')

# Enable Write-Ahead Log journal system
conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL')

# Ensure secure synchronization settings on every commit
conn.execute('PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL')

# Modifications committed below are legally written to disk
conn.execute("INSERT INTO gold_vault VALUES ('vault_A', 5000)")
conn.commit()
